[i]Once you've beat the game with a mask, a star will display next to it and you'll be able to see your best time with this mask.[/i]

[h2]Additions[/h2]
[list][*] Added run timer logic

[*]  Made legger take more time to jump
[*]  Decreased faceless's run speed 
[/list]

[h2]Bug fixes[/h2]
[list][*]  Fixed a display bug when the system's language was german or spanish
[*]  Fixed played dying instantly on taking damage while BUFF in fog with only one heart left
[*]  Fixed some objects being not properly destroy when restarting a run
[*]  Fixed player not losing HAND while idle
[*]  Fixed spike balls being stuck in the air
[*]  Fixed spike balls not damaging enemies sometimes
[*]  Fixed some sounds being played too loudly 
[/list]

notes.title: Mask Around is OUT NOW!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/b3574eb121926844a19668dcf8b39239cd87e16e.png[/img][i]special art I've drawn to celebrate release[/i]

Hello!!! I think today calls for several exclamation marks, because... Well, because it's release day: [b]Mask Around just released[/b]! If you do get the game, it would help me tremendously if you left a review. Early reviews are by far the biggest boost a freshly released Steam game can get.

My work on Mask Around isn't done yet: I still need to release the android version, and I will offer support for bug fixes or game improvements if necessary. I will also keep doing efforts to promote the game during the following weeks. I definitely have ideas for new content as well, but It's a bit too soon to think about that...

[h2]Throwing Numbers At You[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/caf4a789fcb1e88aa2902e7eb5863c347a8db821.png[/img]
[i]There can be a lot of numbers in Mask Around. Now, they're invading the devlog![/i]

I think it's a bit early to do a full post-mortem of the project, but I still wanted to take a step back in this devlog. Let's start with numbers!

[list]
[*] 609 github commits
[*] first commit was on Monday, 29th July 2023
[*] That was 465 days ago, or 1 year, 3 months and 17 days
[*] Worked on the nights/weekend up until july, then basically full time
[*] 619 Steam wishlists
[*] 239 demo downloads[/list]
[h2]On Giving Credits[/h2]

In the past, I've used the term "solo dev" to present myself in the context of video game creation. Today, I'm not really comfortable using the term anymore. Here, I want to give you a brief overview of **who really made Mask Around**. Before I do that, I want to bring up my parents, and my socioeconomic context. I was born in an upper-middle class family, both my parents were teachers, and they gave me the education needed to strive in school, which gave me the time and tools to learn how to make games in the first place. I want to thank them here, and acknowledge the privilege and luck it represents. I wish everybody could create like I had the chance to, and there's still a lot of work to be made towards that goal.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/030d8f28e7f1992d9eba213019a56d47b2e6c6f3.png[/img][i]existing in a context[/i]

Now, about Mask Around specifically. Many people helped me. I need to start with my old friends (they're not old, but our friendship is): [b]PeKaNo[/b] and [b]meliméa[/b], who composed the music for the game. They listened to my intentions and feedback, and put a part of themselves in the universe I had envisioned. I want to thank them here, as they had a lot of impact on the feel of the game.

Localization was another aspect of the game where I got help from two other important people. I knew Mask Up, as a free android game, had some players from Turkey and Russia, so both of these languages were interesting to support. My friend [b]Heretic Burger[/b], who had already translated Mask Up in Turkish, accepted to do it again for Mask Around, and my also very good friend [b]sdjibe[/b] accepted to handle Russian localization. This took hours of work, since Mask Around has more than 1000 words. I'm really grateful for their work, and want to thank them here. I also need to mention two members of my discord server who proofread and added notes to the translations: [b]Brogolem35[/b] for Turkish and [b]Kringe Master[/b] for Russian (discord has been recently banned from both Russia and Turkiye, so I hope this devlog gets to them eventually). All these efforts should allow more people to enjoy the game.

Then, there's everyone who supported me during the development by testing the game and giving me feedback. Among the more active testers and advisors were my friends [b]Paul[/b], [b]ShovelBear[/b] and [b]pandametal[/b]. They definitely guided me well on some decisions, and the game wouldn't be the same without their input and encouragement.
I want to finish this round of thanks with my sisters, who helped me setting up my booth at Sorbonne Play Festival and for their lasting support. There's also a lot of other people, including all the testers, that I couldn't list all here: you can check the in-game credits for the full list. Thank you, everyone!!

[h2]On Embracing Collectiveness[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/169efa8df7702aa0c3cda1561fe7ebddf32d9773.png[/img]
[i]debug screenshot from All That Glitters, a narrative fishing sim I've been working on with a team[/i]

I want to get back to the "solo dev" concept, as I believe its criticism deserves a bit more depth. At the risk of doing cheap leftist politics, I'll say that the solo dev narrative is especially appealing in the context of the rising liberalism around us: every individual must prove itself and prove its value. We're being individualized in many aspects of our lives: everything is becoming an open free market in which everyone needs to compete, under the false pretense of fairness. I believe it has many negative consequences: rising loneliness, communities dissolving, failure to address systemic issues or even social policies being reduced (like the french unemployment benefits, which allowed me to create Mask Around [url=https://www.canardpc.com/jeu-video/dossier-jeu-video/comment-lassurance-chomage-tient-la-scene-inde-a-bout-de-bras/]as well as many other games[/url], that is tuned down every couple of years by the government).

I believe the only way out of this is collective, rather than a solo buzz. Which is why I want to be part of more collective projects in the future. My first step in this direction is teaming up with some friend to create a game together. We're actually in the finishing phase of All That Glitters, a french narrative fishing game that you can [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3288100/All_That_Glitters]wishlist right now[/url].

[h2]On Finding The Meaning Of Life[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/c9eba7d5023a9d51f01b2e8883780d16d2978cac.png[/img]
[i]Photo I took a few years ago, that I used in my [url=https://youtu.be/j_MqFa6JWEU?si=3BqM0bG3QdEeup_y]"random objects I've put in my game" video series[/url][/i]

I've actually been thinking about this a lot recently, and I think I overthinked so hard that I found the meaning of life. They are actually two: [b]artistic creation[/b] and [b]having a valued role in a community[/b]. Mask Around provided the first one for me for many months. I held onto this sense very tight. I knew that this project gave me purpose, albeit temporarily. I've talked with many peers and friends my age, that feel a bit lost in life, that do not find a lot of meaning in their jobs or in their life. I don't know what next year will be made of for now... But whatever happens, I will try to make creation a fair place in my life.

But enough thinking about the future and the past. Tonight, I'll celebrate with my friends who helped me make this game.

Thank you for reading, thank you for supporting,

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2849230/Mask_Around/]Buy Mask Around[/url], follow me [url=https://linktr.ee/maskaround]in other places[/url], subscribe to [url=http://eepurl.com/iLSAec]my newsletter[/url] to stay in touch with me,
[i]and see you around[/i]

                Rouli

notes.title: Steam Next Fest + Release date!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/462d3cb7c12e4c5d7f3b59254cc2bbd3dd2c5853.gif[/img]
[i]cool gif from the new trailer!![/i]

Hey there, fellow devlog readers! Long time no see. Autumn is kicking in, the days are rainy, and you feel like you need some vivid colors in your life? Well, here's a good news for you: [b]Mask Around will be available on [u]November 8th[/u] on Steam[/b]!!! Isn't that exciting? I think it is. Yay!

[h3]On participating in a virtual festival[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/3f0c6d9464b06a67adb4c39699a78ed8f1e096d7.png[/img]
[i]They gave us this template to communicate on the Next Fest so I'm putting it to good use[/i]

Can't wait to play? Well, you're in luck: Mask Around is participating in Steam Next Fest starting... today! Try out the freshly updated demo, and take a look at the awesome new trailer for the game, all that from the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2849230/Mask_Around/]Steam page[/url]. Wishlists, page visits and demo downloads are especially appreciated during this time, because they boost the game's visibility on the platform. I'm currently sitting on ~300 wishlists, which is cool but not a lot at all by indie games standards. So any click helps!

[h3]On participating in a real life festival[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/612d113bc70b5266156409fb3f4bf2e86baa753d.png[/img]
[i]Me at the Play Sorbonne Festival. Thankfully, I've gotten less socially anxious over the years![/i]

A few weeks ago I was also a participant of the Play Sorbonne Festival, an all-things-gaming student-made festival here in Paris. I had a booth where people could play the game and chat with us. I was surprised to receive so many good feedback from so many different kind of people! Some players even came back later in the day just for a chance to play again. I also had some addicted children that didn't want to let go the controller (which was really weird for me to experience! ... should kids play this  game?).  I received the help of friend and family, and my sister even made a creepy life-sized mask as a decoration. I want to thank again to everyone that helped me or came by for support. This definitely boosted my motivation to clear the last remaining issues and actually release the game!

[h3]Putting the last pieces together[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/707ddcad8553bf002b9521bc0ce18fb671b4af26.png[/img]
[i]One of my first drafts for the supernova-themed final boss! Will you manage to beat it?[/i]

Since my last devlog, I've been adding the remaining pieces to Mask Around, namely:
[list] [*]Made an epic final boss[/*][*]Added more level patterns[/*][*]Added the remaining masks and backpacks[/*] [/list]
I've finally reached all of my objectives content-wise, with a whopping 24 masks (with unique powers) and 24 backpacks (purely cosmetic) hidden in the game. I'm also quite proud of the final battle, themed around the sun becoming a supernova... I can't wait to see it in the players' hands!

As usual, if you want to help me, you can [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2849230/Mask_Around/]wishlist Mask Around on Steam[/url], [url=http://eepurl.com/iLSAec]subscribe to my newsletter[/url] or follow me on [url=https://linktr.ee/maskaround]the social media of your choosing[/url]! I’ve been sharing a lot of videos lately, showcasing the different items in the game, so this might interest you.

Anyway, thank you for reading, and see you in a few weeks... for release day!

Rouli

notes.title: Making A Body Without Organs (Steam Demo!)
notes.content:
[h2]No Organs Here[/h2]

Have you ever dreamed about making a [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_without_organs]Body without organs[/url]?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/33db55f8af5f028bf694e794ed2b3d2319a3e586.png[/img]
[i]Buff form (bullet glitch not included)[/i]

While trying to understand this philosophical concept the other day, I realized that maybe this is what my games, and especially Mask Up, are about: enabling the embodiment of something that goes beyond what our simple physical bodies are, or even what they could be. Becoming fluid. In Mask Up, you were directly the juice, while in Mask Around, you begin as a human but slowly become one with the juice, until you reach your final weirdly buffed form, the latest addition to the game.

[h2]Try It Now![/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/09184583203e23327745d621e2ba9f5145861327.png[/img]
[i]I just slapped a big "DEMO" on top of the base art for the Steam promo art.[/i]

As you can see, development have been going smoothly, and I now consider myself nearly done content-wise for release. I can't wait for you to get your hands on the final game... In the meantime, you can try the brand new Steam Demo! It is rather limited in content, as only the first zone is accessible, but it features the new buff form! I let my friend PeKaNo loose on the music, and they did some heavy breakcore remix of the base music... I might have to tune it down a little, but let me know your thoughts!

[h2]Near The End[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/23f4177e60489404ef242d68f2bb1607cfcf5912.png[/img]
[i]This is where the main character keeps his underwear #lore[/i]

This may be my final devlog before the release of Mask Around... I started this project just over one year ago, and it's finally coming to an end (?). I'm feeling a mix of excitement and fear. I reasonably hope that it will a least make a few people happy. I'm still working on the final boss and on end-game content; these moments feel important in my gamedev life, I'll try to enjoy them. See you very soon!

Like usual, you can [url=https://discord.gg/CjncnJtMmr]join the discord server[/url], [url=http://eepurl.com/iLSAec]subscribe to my mailing list[/url] and most importantly, wishlist the game on Steam. Cheers!

Rouli

notes.title: Many Reasons To Explode: Mask Around devlog #2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/eebdf2ec1940b2960e9e040b98239872318019df.png[/img]
[h2]Following the fun : first zone rework[/h2]
Lately, I've been trying to "follow the fun" with Mask Around. I realized that what I found fun in platformer roguelike is the principle of "chain of action": one action leading to another, which leads to another, and so on. I've been tweaking the game and adding small mechanics in order to extends existing chains of action.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/281da3c2e8c3468e7c24d54061fda7847a64a995.gif[/img]
[i]gif #1: action > reaction > more reaction[/i]

For this, I've added an explosive variant of the green blocs. These new deadly obstacles explode when something collides with them with a strong enough impact. Secondly, I've modified the drone behavior so that it explodes upon death. Both of these mechanics can be a danger for the player, as well as an opportunity, since the explosions damage enemies as well. I also took the time to add secrets, namely masks and backpacks, with a focus on the first area. I'm pretty proud of the result!

[h2]Zone 2: Clover for cover[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/8649be8de27afb8f90f247903975795f4d85a0bc.gif[/img]
[i]gif #2: Clover bloc in action[/i]

I also began working on the second zone, which is themed around plants. The main mechanic of the zone is the clover bloc, which acts as a perfect gear in the "chain of action" described above. Any damage will trigger the clover switch, which will then make the clover bloc follow its path. It can be used as a platform, a trap, for some cover, ... In the current build, it's still very buggy, but I can't wait to show you the many uses for this bloc. [url=https://mastodon.gamedev.place/@rouli/112438691226234157]Here's some more footage[/url] of the new zone and the clover bloc in action. My friend PeKaNo really outdid himself on the music.

[h2]The Road Ahead[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/389ae13a6df87b4f911af6d62b726521ff971dc5.png[/img]
[i]Third form concept[/i]

The game is really taking shape! I've also taken the time to do boring stuff, like adding controller support in menus, fixing bugs, improving UI... The remaining big features I need to add in order to finish the game are:
[list]
[*] Finishing zone 2 (adding one enemy + one semi boss)
[*] Reworking zone 3 (adding a mechanic + one semi boss)
[*] Adding a final boss
[*] Adding third playable form
[/list]

I'm hoping to do all that in the following months for a 2024 release. If you haven't done so already, you can wishlist the game, [url=https://discord.gg/SjUzzr3wr9]join the discord channel[/url] or [url=http://eepurl.com/iLSAec]subscribe to the newsletter[/url] to receive these devlog directly in your mailbox (with some added bonus).

Thanks for reading and [i]see you around[/i]!

notes.title: The Idea That Came To Me In A Fever Dream
notes.content:
So... I've been working on this game for the last 8 months and I today I'm finally announcing it! In this post I want to talk about what is Mask Around and why I'm making it. But first check out the trailer:
[previewyoutube=I9N3D0Z1r6Q;full][/previewyoutube]

In 2019, I created Mask Up, a mobile roguelike, that I [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1537430/Mask_Up/]ported to Steam later[/url]. With Mask Up, my goal was to make a platformer with only two buttons. I made several moveset to experiment with this fun but limiting control scheme, which ended up being the 4 playable forms. Mask Up was an experimental game from the beginning: fun to develop, but somewhat messy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/8e2a291bd9fcfc9fea05f8c3c280a0db9306c65f.png[/img]
[i]the infamous 'Mask Up' and 'Plant Down' characters[/i]

Two years later, I naturally wanted to created something more polished, so I started working on Plant Down, a short Mask Up prequel that consisted of only 3 boss fights. The two button control scheme was kept unchanged, but I simplified the moveset a lot: only one attack and a fixed jump height. I was pretty happy with the result, and thought I was done with the two-button gimmick.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/51293c9e51d522858cd45f47c5bd5a3cad8fb2c3.png[/img]
[i]The precise moment where I got the idea for Mask Around[/i]

But last summer, during a hot night (I sleep under the roof of an old parisian building, it gets very hot during the summer without AC), I found myself thinking about it again, about this whole two buttons adventure from 5 years ago. But what was there to do now? Then, an idea struck: I could use the phone gyroscope, on top of the two buttons, to add a fun twist without changing the core concept.

[h2]A twisted Idea[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/a875a845639e3053198233d2be7328ce488fb1f3.png[/img]
[i]The sexy prototype of Mask Around[/i]

So, the day after that night (because it's still important to sleep), I began furiously prototyping. And soon enough, I was playing this idea, and it felt really nice. Over the course of the following months of work I realized several things:
[list]
[*]     I couldn't only use gyroscope for aiming since many low-end phone actually don't have one
[*]     I needed to have a PC version in mind from the start if I wanted it to be successful
[/list]
So I took the time to develop extra input support, that don't use the original two buttons input that started it all. The game feels really great now with a controller or with keyboard + mouse, even though I was reticent for a long time and wanted to keep it an android exclusive. So I guess the lesson is sometimes it's good to change your mind? Thanks to these efforts, I can now do marketing properly because I know the game runs well on PC, and this is why you're reading this right now (how does it feels to get marketed towards? I bet it feels nice.)

[h2]The Highly Strategical Roadmap[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44927911/39d72f5ca6fd62869b7011eca68aec0fe3de461b.png[/img]
[i]Some wacky items from the game that will surely make you buy it.[/i]

Content wise, I'm aiming for the following at launch:
[list]
[*]     3 major biomes with a unique mechanic and set of enemies each
[*]     3 minor secret biomes
[*]     One final boss
[*]     Something like 16 items, 8 weapons, 16 masks, 16 cosmetics backpacks.
[/list]
Right now, I'd say I made 50% of my goal. I plan on launching early and add content post-launch through free updates. But it will depend on my situation at that time and on the game's reception. So if that something you'd want, please support the game as much as you can: wishlist it on Steam, share it with friends, send me anonymous letters with enormous amount of cash!

Thanks a lot for reading! I intend on making more of these devlogs on various topics, so let me know if there are particular topics you want me to cover. See you around!

Rouli

PS: Oh, and by the way, I'm running a big discount on Mask Up right now if you want to try it! https://store.steampowered.com/app/1537430/Mask_Up/
